clue.text: Zulu loses head in war dance

indicators.note: losing its head means the name's first letter is dropped

parts.note: Shaka was the most famous Zulu king, so the Zulu here is that name

explanation.surface: A Zulu warrior is knocked out of a ceremonial dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zulu' looks like the NATO word for Z; it is the Zulu king SHAKA, and 'loses head' drops his S.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is the Maori ceremonial challenge performed before battle, and now before rugby matches.

clue.text: Juliett with a gong touring rock festival

indicators.note: here the NATO word Juliett stands for its initial letter, J, which 'with' attaches to the rest
touring means going all the way round, so the honour encloses the rock

parts.note: a gong is slang for a medal or honour, here the MBE
ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Someone called Juliett takes a gong on tour around a rock festival.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for an honour such as the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire); 'touring' wraps it round the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large lively gathering or celebration, such as a scout rally.

clue.text: People like ones regularly seen around the borders of India

indicators.note: seen around means the preceding letters sit either side of what follows

parts.note: as means like, in 'as good as gold'

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word ones is taken
the borders of a word are its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: People resembling individuals regularly spotted along India's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' puts the first pair of pieces either side of India's outer letters; 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'ones'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asians are the people of Asia, a group named as a whole, as India's neighbours are.

clue.text: 16D Rue Simon is an address in Quebec

indicators.note: the answer to 16 down is TAILORED, meaning altered, so the street name is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A street name, Rue Simon, offered as a postal address in French-speaking Quebec.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 16 down supplies the anagram signal: the letters of RUE SIMON are tailored, i.e. altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsieur is the French form of address for a man, used in French-speaking Quebec.

clue.text: Nurse in Lima adjusted routine

indicators.note: in places the nurse within the rearranged letters
adjusted means the letters of Lima are rearranged

parts.note: EN is short for enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse working in Lima has had her routine adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges Lima to MIAL; 'in' then sets the nurse inside, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Menial work is humdrum and unskilled, the routine drudgery of a job.

clue.text: Lots of bottoms in Last Tango In Paris

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottoms of words are their last letters, taken from each in turn

explanation.surface: Plenty of bare bottoms on show in the film Last Tango in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of Last, Tango, In, Paris spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tons is informal for a great quantity, as in 'tons of time'.

clue.text: Papa is leader of men's movement

parts.note: dada is a child's word for father, that is papa

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Father is the head of a men's campaign group.
explanation.walkthrough: Papa is also the NATO word for P, a red herring here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dadaism was the early twentieth-century anti-art movement in painting and poetry.

clue.text: Cosmetic surgery for man's penis performed by Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner is the clergyman who swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two sounds trade places

parts.note: Joe's is a man's, Joe being a typical man's name
knob is British slang for penis

explanation.surface: A cheeky request for cosmetic surgery on a man's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: JOE'S KNOB with starting sounds swapped says NOSE JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose job is informal for rhinoplasty, plastic surgery that reshapes the nose.

clue.text: Show off going round in uniform

indicators.note: going round means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to brag is to show off

explanation.surface: Someone showing off as they parade around in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing of a distinctive kind, such as a uniform or official dress.

clue.text: Two muppets in show's opening getting bravos

parts.note: muppet is British slang for a fool, as is ass, and two of them stand side by side

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pair of puppets at the start of a show get cheers of 'bravo'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bravos' looks like applause, but it is the plural of bravo, a hired thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A bravo is a hired killer or ruffian, so bravos are paid murderers.

clue.text: Dual carriageway over sierra is most unnatural

indicators.note: over means the two streets lie across, either side of, the range

parts.note: ST, street, is a carriageway, and dual calls for two of them
a sierra is a mountain range

explanation.surface: A dual carriageway running over a mountain is the strangest sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra looks like the NATO word for S, but here it means a mountain range, which 'over' lets the two streets straddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd or abnormal, so the strangest is the most unnatural of all.

clue.text: Traditions rose up after 5th of November

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the single letter
the 5th of a word is its fifth letter
up as in stirred up means the letters of rose are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Traditions sprang up after Bonfire Night, the 5th of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals an anagram of rose. The 5th of November is Bonfire Night in Britain, a deliberate decoy; here it is the fifth letter of the word November.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the established customs and conventions of a society.

clue.text: Virile, but motionless?

definitions.meaning: Mach 0, Mach zero, is a speed of nothing, so something at it is motionless

explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes overt masculinity; Mach is a speed measured against sound.

clue.text: Bloom's outspoken after whiskey meal

indicators.note: after puts the spoken word following the whiskey

parts.note: rye is an American whiskey

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so the word for bloom is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a bloom is a flower

explanation.surface: Someone called Bloom speaks frankly after a whiskey-fuelled meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey is also NATO's W, a decoy. 'meal' is ground grain, not dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye flour is ground grain, and meal is a coarse ground grain.

clue.text: Open a French letter

parts.note: un is French for a
a cap is a capital letter

explanation.surface: An invitation to open a French letter, British slang for a condom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French letter' is old British slang for a condom; the clue splits it into 'a French' and 'letter'.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap is to take the lid off, so to open a bottle or pen.

clue.text: Echo distorted the line

indicators.note: distorted means the letters of echo are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An echo bounced back distorted along the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Echo also suggests the NATO E, but here it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line a darts player stands behind when throwing.

clue.text: Singer's ring captured by X-ray at first

indicators.note: captured by puts the ring between the other two pieces, held in their grasp

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of ray

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A singer's ring is caught on an X-ray at the first examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X-ray' is NATO's X, but the clue splits it: X is TEN and ray's first letter R, with O between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, the part between alto and baritone.

clue.text: Modified Rio delta variant

indicators.note: a variant is a different version, so the letters of Rio delta take a new order

explanation.surface: A modified Rio delta, a variant of the river's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Delta is also the NATO D; here its letters are anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailored means adapted or altered to suit a purpose, so modified.

clue.text: Nick comes back with kilo of snacks

indicators.note: comes back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to nick is to make a small cut

explanation.surface: Nick returns carrying a kilo of snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for sweets and snacks; Kilo is also NATO's K.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British, especially school, slang for food eaten as snacks, as in a tuck shop.

clue.text: Drink with golf partner in bag store

parts.note: tea is a drink
a caddy accompanies a golfer and carries the clubs

explanation.surface: A drink with a golfing partner, a store in one's golf bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf is NATO's G, a decoy. 'bag store' means a store for teabags, not a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small container for keeping tea, so teabags are stored in it.

clue.text: Sensible to embrace Love Island and behave like Romeo

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold inside, so the sensible word goes round the rest

parts.note: wise means sensible
love is zero in tennis, written O
Man is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A sensible person signs up for the TV dating show Love Island and behaves like Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality dating show. Romeo is NATO's R, but here is Shakespeare's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To womanise is to chase many women, acting as a romantic lover like Shakespeare's Romeo.

clue.text: Book Alfa Romeo battery recharge

parts.note: Alfa is the NATO alphabet word for A
Romeo is the NATO alphabet word for R
a rest is a pause to recharge one's batteries

explanation.surface: An Alfa Romeo car is booked in for a battery recharge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is not a volume: it is a verb, the police booking an offender.
explanation.definitionFit: To book someone is for police to charge them, close to arresting them.

clue.text: Victor Hugo's beginning to get into party

indicators.note: to get into means the letter goes inside the word for party

parts.note: a camp is a group or party with shared views

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Victor Hugo starts to get involved in a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Hugo is the French novelist; Victor is also NATO's V. Both are decoys.
explanation.definitionFit: A champ, short for champion, is a winner, which is what a victor is.

clue.text: Reprimand from Oscar Peterson

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken from inside the following words, across the gap

explanation.surface: A telling-off from the jazz pianist Oscar Peterson.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar is also NATO's O; here it is the jazz pianist's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British informal for reprimanding them, from being called onto the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Yankee statesman is surprisingly "Mr Everton"

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters of Mr Everton turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A US politician is unexpectedly nicknamed after Everton football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club. 'statesman' is a man of a state, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vermonter is a native of Vermont, a New England state; New Englanders are Yankees.

clue.text: Beastly rival acquiring hotel at last

indicators.note: acquiring means the word for rival takes in the next letter

parts.note: to vie is to compete, to rival

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of hotel

explanation.surface: A nasty rival buys up a hotel in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotel is also NATO's H, but here only its last letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Vile and beastly both mean extremely unpleasant or nasty.

clue.text: Surrounded by the morning papers

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means morning
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone sits surrounded by the morning newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' suggests newspapers; here it means identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of, so encircled by.

clue.text: Part of Mike Ashley's retail empire

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slice of retail tycoon Mike Ashley's business empire.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Ashley owns the Sports Direct chain; Mike is also NATO's M.
explanation.definitionFit: IKEA is a worldwide Swedish furniture chain, a vast business in shops.

clue.text: Charlie Sheen in audition for group

parts.note: Charlie is the NATO alphabet word for C

indicators.note: in audition means heard, so the word for sheen is taken by its sound

parts.note: lustre is a sheen or gloss

explanation.surface: Actor Charlie Sheen trying out at an audition for a group.
explanation.walkthrough: LUSTRE said aloud gives LUSTER, its American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster is a bunch of similar things gathered closely together, a group.

clue.text: Twirls following foxtrot finale, revealing underwear

indicators.note: following puts the twirls after the single letter
the finale of a word is its last letter

parts.note: eddies are swirling currents, twirls

explanation.surface: A dancer's twirls after the foxtrot's finish show off her underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Foxtrot is also NATO's F; here only its last letter, T, counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddies are one-piece women's undergarments combining camisole and knickers.
